feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Fed expected to raise interest rates. And, board votes to close Kennedy Center
entry.summary: The Fed is expected to raise interest rates today for the first time in three years. And, the Kennedy Center board voted yesterday to close the historic center.

entry.title: EU's Ursula von der Leyen says she wants Canada to become an associate member
entry.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed making Canada the European Union's first associate member, a striking overture as U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs drive Ottawa closer to Europe.

entry.title: Senators question Trump's picks for top health positions, including surgeon general
entry.summary: On Wednesday, the Senate committee on health holds a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third attempt to nominate a surgeon general.

entry.title: Kosovo's ex-President Thaci convicted of war crimes, sentenced to 25 years in prison
entry.summary: A European Union-backed court convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes committed during his country's war for independence from Serbia and sentenced him to 25 years in prison.

entry.title: Saudi Arabia calls an attempted Mecca attack a 'red line' as Houthis deny they did it
entry.summary: Saudi Arabia accused Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels overnight of trying to attack Islam's holiest city, prompting condemnation from countries in the region but no sign of military support.

entry.title: As campaign season gears up, AI-generated ads are everywhere
entry.summary: Data suggests many candidates are embracing AI this year to boost their image and portray their opponents unfavorably. But whether it will turn out voters remains unclear.

entry.title: A Kansas girl ran off to join the circus and changed the tattoo world
entry.summary: One of the country's first known female tattoo artists was born on a Kansas farm. Maud Stevens Wagner ran off to join the circus and later became a tattoo legend.

entry.title: The Fed is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in 3 years
entry.summary: The Fed is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate to combat stubborn inflation. That could make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or carry a balance on a credit card.

entry.title: New maps reveal massive gaps in access to affordable birth control across the U.S
entry.summary: Because of a data lag, the current reality of access may be even worse.

entry.title: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
entry.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.
